title: bug: get_activity_log reads only the live activity.log, so after each 10 MB rotation every older event drops out of filtered and unfiltered queries (and the IDE Activity panel) while search.complete reports true, against MCP_SERVER.md's 5000-recent-line scan
description:
Filed by hunt task-afe61cc0 (2026-11-03 #11, lane 2: daemon read/query tools).

PROBLEM
- getActivityLogWindow (packages/moe-daemon/src/state/activityLog.ts:204-216) reads only .moe/activity.log, through readLastLinesWithMetadata. Nothing reads the rotated generations.
- LogRotator.rotate (src/util/LogRotator.ts:82-113) gzips the whole live log into activity.log.1.gz and truncates it once it passes LOG_MAX_SIZE_MB (default 10), keeping LOG_RETENTION_COUNT (default 5) generations.
- So right after every rotation, get_activity_log answers only from the events appended since. queryActivityLog (src/tools/getActivityLog.ts:117-122) fetches 5000 lines for a filtered query and offset+limit+1 for an unfiltered one, and both stop at the live file.
- getActivityLog.ts:174 reports `search.complete: !scanned.hasMoreOlderLines`, which is true whenever the live file is shorter than the fetch. A caller is told the search was complete, and unfiltered paging reports hasMore:false at the rotation boundary.
- This contradicts docs/MCP_SERVER.md's moe.get_activity_log note ("Filtered queries scan at most 5000 recent lines; older matches are not returned") and the comment at getActivityLog.ts:140-144 ("Truncation is still surfaced via search.complete/scanLimit").
- The IDE Activity panel takes the same path: /ws GET_ACTIVITY_LOG calls queryActivityLog (src/server/WebSocketServer.ts:436-443).

EVIDENCE
1. Repro on HEAD 31492ac5, run in a git-archive snapshot outside the shared checkout: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-afe61cc0/B/zzHuntB_activityRotation.test.ts, verbatim output in zzHuntB_activityRotation.output.txt. It logs a task-a event, rotates with `new LogRotator(logPath, { maxSizeMB: 0.0001 }).rotateIfNeeded()`, logs a task-b event and queries {taskId:'task-a'}:
   {"rotated":true,"files":["activity.log","activity.log.1.gz"],"liveLines":2,"filteredByTaskA":{"returned":0,"hasMore":false,"search":{"scannedEvents":2,"scannedLines":2,"scanLimit":5000,"matchingEventsWithinScan":0,"complete":true}},"unfiltered":{"returned":2,"hasMore":false,"complete":true}}
2. Live .moe, 2026-11-03: the log rotated at 09:13Z and 19:12Z. At 20:40Z:
   - the live activity.log held 896 lines, the first stamped 2026-11-03T19:12:21.618Z;
   - activity.log.1.gz held 4,036 lines (09:13:53Z to 19:12:18Z);
   - activity.log.2.gz held 4,441 lines (2026-11-02T21:41Z to 2026-11-03T09:13Z).
   So a governor or QA query for anything earlier today (a claim, a plan approval, a QA verdict) returns nothing with complete:true, though it lies well inside a 5000-line scan.

FIX DIRECTION
- When the live file yields fewer lines than the fetch, continue newest-first into activity.log.1.gz, .2.gz and so on (zlib gunzip, up to LOG_RETENTION_COUNT) until the fetch is met.
- Set hasMoreOlderLines whenever a line or a generation is left unread, so search.complete and unfiltered hasMore stay honest.
- Keep the 5000-line budget, the newest-first order and the response shape.
- Skip an unreadable or corrupt .gz with a logged warning, report complete:false for it, and never throw from the query.
- Stop decompressing once the fetch is met. At about 4,000 lines a generation, a full filtered scan reads the live file plus one or two generations.
- No StateManager.ts edit is needed (task-34e42a0a may hold it).
- Do not edit docs/MCP_SERVER.md (task-0adea941 holds it): the fix makes its note true.

FILES
- packages/moe-daemon/src/state/activityLog.ts
- packages/moe-daemon/src/util/reverseReader.ts, only if a shared line reader helps
- new packages/moe-daemon/src/state/activityLog.rotation.test.ts

implementationPlan.description:
Fix packages/moe-daemon/src/state/activityLog.ts. This is the only runtime file. getActivityLog.ts, StateManager.ts, reverseReader.ts, LogRotator.ts and docs/MCP_SERVER.md stay unchanged; 0adea941 holds the doc, and the fix makes its 5000-recent-line note true.

Changes:
- import zlib.
- Add MAX_ROTATED_GENERATIONS = 50 and MAX_ROTATED_BYTES = 64 MiB. Comment: 6x the 10 MB default rotation size; a larger or hostile generation is skipped, not inflated.
- Add a private readActivityTail(logPath, limit) that returns { lines (oldest first), hasMoreOlderLines }:
  - Read the live file with readLastLinesWithMetadata.
  - Then, while !hasMoreOlderLines, walk n = 1, 2, ... over `${logPath}.${n}.gz`, the LogRotator naming, newest first.
  - Stop at the first missing generation: rotate() keeps the generations contiguous.
  - If the window is already full (lines.length >= limit) or n > MAX_ROTATED_GENERATIONS, set hasMoreOlderLines = true and stop, because an older generation is still unread.
  - Otherwise read the generation: zlib.gunzipSync(fs.readFileSync(gz), { maxOutputLength: MAX_ROTATED_BYTES }), utf-8, split on /\r?\n/, drop empty lines.
  - Let need = limit - lines.length. It is always > 0 here, so slice(-need) never becomes slice(-0). Prepend older.slice(-need), and set hasMoreOlderLines when older.length > need.
- Error handling: a generation that cannot be read or decompressed is skipped. That covers a corrupt file, one truncated mid-rotation, and one over the cap. Log logger.warn({ error, gzPath }, 'Skipping unreadable rotated activity log'), record a gap and continue to the next older generation. The gap forces hasMoreOlderLines true, so search.complete reads false. getActivityLogWindow keeps its outer try/catch and still never throws.
- In getActivityLogWindow:
  - Drop the fs.existsSync(logPath) early return. A missing live file reads as zero lines (readLastLinesWithMetadata handles that), and the generations are still read.
  - Call readActivityTail where readLastLinesWithMetadata was called.
  - Leave the parse, validate, reverse, slice and linesRead code as it is.
- Update the header comment (lines 11-15) and the function doc to say the rotated generations are read.

Design choices:
- No cache of decompressed generations, so memory stays flat; this epic's history includes an activity-log OOM.
- Decompression stops once the window is full.
- Measured on this board: a 10 MiB generation (~4,000 lines) inflates and splits in ~51-54 ms. A filtered query, whose live file always holds fewer than 5000 lines, therefore pays about 50 ms more under the MCP mutex. /ws GET_ACTIVITY_LOG asks for at most 101 lines.

The reference diff (read-only) is /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-05a77c0d/activityLog.fix.diff. With it the new file passes 8/8, and the architect's mutants were each killed:
- a plain `break` at the full-window branch: (r5);
- dropping `|| gap`: (r6);
- `continue` replaced by `break` on a bad generation: (r6);
- `>` replaced by `>=`: (r7);
- slice(-need) replaced by slice(need): 7 cases.

Applied with Edit (+43/-5). No cache, no other file touched.

implementationPlan.note: Adversarial self-review (no edits). (a) Concurrent rotation: scratch run shows zlib.gunzipSync throws Z_BUF_ERROR on a gzip truncated mid-stream, on one missing its trailer, and on an empty .gz; ERR_BUFFER_TOO_LARGE past maxOutputLength. Each lands in the per-generation catch: logger.warn, gap, complete:false, no throw. No duplicate lines, because the live log still holds them until the truncate. A generation renamed away between existsSync and readFileSync gives ENOENT, caught the same way. Known transient window, not fixed (plan says stop at the first missing generation; no scope growth): in rotate(), between the shift loop and the new .1.gz being created (sub-ms to a few ms), .1.gz is missing while .2.gz exists, so a query in that window can report complete:true from the still-intact live log. A retry heals it. (b) A generation over 64 MiB, or hostile, is refused by maxOutputLength and skipped. Worst-case transient peak is the inflated buffer plus string plus split lines, only when LOG_MAX_SIZE_MB is near 60; the 10 MB default is about 50 MB. (c) limit 0 or negative still hits the safeLimit===0 early return; normalize() clamps the limit; a deep unfiltered page (offset+limit+1 ~ 10k lines) reads about 3 generations, each stopped once the window is full. (d) Module-level state is two numeric constants; no decompressed data survives a call. (e) git status: only activityLog.ts (M) and activityLog.rotation.test.ts (new). (f) No forbiddenPatterns string in added lines or in the new test. Empty .gz (zero lines) is a valid generation: older=[] and the walk continues.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: moe.get_activity_log and /ws GET_ACTIVITY_LOG read the newest lines across .moe/activity.log and its rotated activity.log.<n>.gz generations, newest first. Reading stops once the fetch is met: 5000 lines for a filtered query, offset+limit+1 for an unfiltered one. search.complete is false, and an unfiltered page reports hasMore, exactly when older lines remain unread or a generation could not be read. Otherwise search.complete is true.
invariants: The response shape, the newest-first order and ACTIVITY_LOG_FILTER_SCAN_LIMIT (5000) are unchanged.
getActivityLogWindow never throws. An unreadable generation is logged, skipped and reported as complete:false.
No decompressed generation is retained between calls, and each generation's inflate is capped at 64 MiB.
The reader never writes, renames or deletes anything under .moe/.
compatibility: The existing tests getActivityLog, reverseReader, LogRotator, initHookFixes (which mocks getActivityLogWindow), activityActor and StateManager pass unchanged.
docs/MCP_SERVER.md is not edited (held by 0adea941). Its 'Filtered queries scan at most 5000 recent lines' note becomes true across rotations.
reuse: readLastLinesWithMetadata, unchanged, for the live file.
zlib.gunzipSync with maxOutputLength for the generations. gzip cannot be read backwards, so a whole-generation inflate is unavoidable, and a sync call keeps the /ws handler synchronous.
The LogRotator naming, rather than a second copy of its env parsing.

approachesConsidered: Streaming gunzip with a ring buffer of the last N lines was rejected: getActivityLogWindow is synchronous and the /ws handler uses it synchronously, and a stream still has to inflate the whole generation.
A cache of the decompressed .1.gz keyed by mtime and size was rejected because it would retain 10+ MB per daemon, and this epic's history includes an activity-log OOM.
Bounding the walk with LOG_RETENTION_COUNT was rejected because it duplicates LogRotator's env parsing. A walk that stops at the first missing generation, with a hard cap of 50, needs neither.

risks: Each filtered query pays about 50 ms more on this board, under the MCP mutex.
LOG_MAX_SIZE_MB above about 60 makes generations exceed the 64 MiB cap. They are then skipped with a warning and complete:false: a deliberate degrade, explained in the code comment.
